text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Heated accusations of bribery between two parliamentary deputies during discussion over whether new television law should include a clause about the principles of the Great Arab Revolt.
- Arafat sends message to King Hussein; prime minister affirms Jordan's support for Palestinians.
- minister of supply sets up committee to look into the case of imported wheat which unfit for human consumption.
- Palestinian sources say Israel is preparing a plan for religious rather than political administration of Jerusalem to resolve dispute over the city.
- Crown Prince Hassan says Israel's settlement decision creates an air of pessimism around the peace process.
- Parliament to discuss the Israeli settlements today.
- Israeli-Palestinian talks have fallen apart and the spectre of violence dominates.
- Swiss delegation arrives in Jordan to invite eight blue-chip firms to investment conference in London.
- Prime minister reiterates Jordan's support for Palestinian stand.
